verifiedBy: Claude (lane A engineer, Scope 3 completion I-12u), 2026-10-30; built by tools/method-reference/build_scope3_us_upstream_register.py from the committed transcription files
method: US upstream register R5 for Scope 3 category 3 activities A (upstream of purchased fuels), B (upstream of purchased electricity), C (upstream of electricity lost in transmission and distribution) and D (upstream of energy resold). Hand transcriptions (WebFetch, two verbatim reads that agreed; transcription webfetch_double_read) of free official documents, each entry citing publisher, title, edition, URL, page/table/row and both quotes: NETL DOE/NETL-2024/4862 natural gas supply chain (8.8 production through distribution, 7.8 production through transmission, g CO2e/MJ, HHV, IPCC AR6 100-year as published); CA-GREET3.0 Lookup Table TSD (2018) Tables A.1, B.1, D.1 (upstream = Total - Tailpipe, component rows asserted within 0.01; GWP set not stated, AR4 inferred and re-verified by arithmetic); CARB LCFS 17 CCR 95486 Table 4 energy densities (LHV, the basis of CA-GREET3.0); eGRID heat-input HHV basis (40 CFR 72.2, EIA). Derived constants are exact. No coal or oil upstream value is registered (none was verifiable). Upgrade each entry to a file read (pdftotext) with a document SHA-256 once the documents are staged. Round 2 (lane F, DESIGN 13.6): a derived, methane-only coal term from EPA GHGI 1990-2022 Table 3-1 (coal mining CH4 2022, AR5) and EIA MER Tables 6.1 and A5 (2022 coal production and its gross heat content), one division rounded half-even to 12 dp; its derivation record is in the provenance sidecar. Round 3 (lane A, owner decision 2): NPC 2011 Table 7 coal upstream combustion (5.0 lb CO2e/MMBtu, AR4) and Abrahams et al. 2015 Table S7 coal upstream (12.2 g CO2e/MJ, non-IPCC GWP) are registered as entries for a screening-range memo of the omitted coal mining energy and transport CO2 only (outside every total; older vintages, heating value not stated).

constants.unit: kg CO2e per MMBtu of coal (HHV; IPCC AR5 100-year; coal mine methane only)
constants.basis: Derived, not a printed value (DESIGN 13.6; derivation record in the provenance sidecar): round12(43.6 MMT CO2e (EPA GHGI 1990-2022 Table 3-1, CH4, Coal Mining, 2022; AR5) x 10^9 kg/MMT / (594,155 thousand short tons (EIA MER Table 6.1, 2022 production) x 1000 x 20.100 MMBtu per short ton (EIA MER Table A5, 2022 coal production, gross heat content))) = 43,600,000,000 / 11,942,515,500, half-even to 12 dp. Methane only: coal mining energy and coal transport CO2 are not included; abandoned mines are excluded; the denominator is all U.S. production, exports included
Definition: 1 million metric tons (MMT) = 10^6 t x 1000 kg/t = 10^9 kg
Definition: International Table Btu = 1055.05585262 J, so 1 MMBtu = 10^6 Btu = 1055.05585262 MJ exactly (the definition behind supplement_const.kwh_per_mmbtu)

entries.unit: definition
labelCells: quote1: Heat input rate means the product (expressed in mmBtu/hr) of the gross calorific value of the fuel (expressed in mmBtu/mass of fuel) and the fuel feed rate into the combustion device (expressed in mass of fuel/hr) and does not include the heat derived from preheated combustion air, recirculated flue gases, or exhaust from other sources.
quote2: Heat input rate means the product (expressed in mmBtu/hr) of the gross calorific value of the fuel  [LII mirror https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/40/72.2]
